mainTopic: Rules of mourning: late news of a death, קריעה, which relatives one mourns for, mourning together with a spouse, and tearing while standing.
overview: The גמרא finishes the story of רב hinting to his uncle רבי חייא that רבי חייא's brother and sister have died. רבי חייא removes his shoes and soon goes to bathe, and the גמרא learns three הלכות from this: an אבל may not wear shoes, late news (שמועה רחוקה) needs only one day of mourning, and part of a day counts as the whole day. News that becomes late during a רגל or שבת also needs only one day. רבי מני and רבי חנינא then argue about whether one does קריעה for late news, and the גמרא explains why tearing for a parent after שבעה does not disprove רבי מני. A ברייתא lists the relatives one mourns for, along with a מחלוקת about mourning for a relative's relatives. The גמרא learns that a husband joins his wife's mourning only for her parents, from the story of מר עוקבא and from ברייתות. Finally, אמימר tears his garment in front of his grieving son and redoes the tear standing, which is learned from the פסוק about איוב.

steps.title: רב hints at the deaths, and רבי חייא begins mourning
steps.stepSummary: רב avoids saying the bad news directly. He answers with questions, and רבי חייא understands that his siblings have died. He removes his shoes and then heads to the bathhouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to him: Is my mother alive? He said to him: Is your mother alive? He said to him: Is my father alive? רבי חייא said to his servant: Take off my shoes, and carry my things after me to the bathhouse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the story. רב uses questions to hint that his own mother and father, who are רבי חייא's sister and brother, have passed away, and רבי חייא reacts by mourning briefly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב did not want to announce the deaths outright, so he answered each question with another question. רבי חייא understood the hint. He took off his shoes, which is a sign of mourning. Right away he went to the bathhouse, which shows his mourning lasted only a short time.

keyTerms.meaning: Mother
Alive, still living
His attendant or servant
Take off (the shoes)
Bathhouse

phrases.english: He (Rav) said to him: Is my mother alive?
phrases.notes: רב's mother was רבי חייא's sister. רב answers a question with a question to avoid saying the sad news.

phrases.english: He (Rabbi Chiya) said to him: Is your mother alive?
He (Rav) said to him: Is my father alive?
He (Rabbi Chiya) said to his servant:
Take off my shoes for me,
and carry my things after me to the bathhouse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a story that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא, hearing late news of his siblings' deaths, removed his shoes and then went to bathe the same day.

steps.title: Three rules learned from Rabbi Chiya's actions
steps.stepSummary: From the story, the גמרא learns three things. An אבל may not wear shoes. Late news requires only one day of mourning. Part of a day counts as a whole day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn three things from this. Learn from this that a mourner is forbidden to wear shoes. Learn that late news is kept for only one day. And learn that part of the day counts like the whole day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes רבי חייא's behavior and draws three practical הלכות from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking off his shoes shows that an אבל may not wear shoes. He heard the news more than thirty days after the deaths, which makes it a שמועה רחוקה. Because he mourned only that one day, we learn that late news needs only one day. Because he bathed right after a short time, we learn that a small part of the day counts as the full day.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; a conclusion drawn from a case
A mourner
Wearing shoes
Late news of a death, heard after thirty days
Part of the day counts like the whole day

steps.whatToRemember: Late news (after thirty days) means only one day of mourning, and even part of that day is enough.
steps.confusionAlert: Each 'שמע מינה' begins a separate rule. The three rules are not one long sentence.
steps.whyThisMatters: These are practical rules of אבלות that come straight from what a great sage actually did.

phrases.english: Learn three things from this.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ — אָבֵל אָסוּר בִּנְעִילַת הַסַּנְדָּל,
phrases.english: Learn from this: a mourner is forbidden to wear shoes,
and learn from this: late news
is kept for only one day,
and learn from this: part of the day is like all of it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws legal conclusions from the story in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: An אבל may not wear shoes; a שמועה רחוקה lasts one day; part of a day counts as the whole day.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא's actions on hearing of his siblings' deaths.

steps.title: רבי חייא and רבי אחייה are two different people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why רבי חייא kept only one day while רבי אחייה kept seven and thirty days. They are simply two different people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא is one person, and רבי אחייה is a separate person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question it does not say out loud. Why did רבי חייא mourn only one day, when רבי אחייה mourned seven and thirty days?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think רבי חייא and רבי אחייה are the same man, because their names sound alike. If so, his two stories would contradict each other. The גמרא says they are two separate people, so there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Separately; a different, distinct one

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי חייא and רבי אחייה. The whole answer is that they are different people.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya is separate,
phrases.notes: The question is left unsaid: an earlier story had רבי אחייה mourn seven and thirty days, not just one.

phrases.english: Rabbi Achiya is separate.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא לְחוּד, רַבִּי אֲחִיָּיה לְחוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles an apparent contradiction between step 2's rule and an earlier story.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identity distinction: the two stories are about different people.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חייא and רבי אחייה are the same person, so his behavior contradicts itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are two different people, so the stories do not contradict.

steps.title: News that becomes late during a Festival
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין rules on someone who hears recent news on a רגל. If thirty days have passed by the time the רגל ends, the רגל days count toward the thirty, and he keeps only one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר אבין said: If one heard recent news during a רגל, and at the end of the רגל it became late news, the רגל counts for him, and he keeps only one day.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. It deals with recent news that turns into late news while the mourner could not mourn because of the רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a רגל one may not mourn. The news was recent (שמועה קרובה) when he heard it. By the end of the רגל, though, thirty days had passed since the death. רבי יוסי בר אבין rules that the רגל days count toward the thirty, so the news is now late and he mourns only one day.

keyTerms.meaning: Recent news of a death, heard within thirty days
A Festival (פסח, שבועות, סוכות)
The end of the Festival
It counts for him

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that days when mourning is not allowed still count toward the thirty days.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin said:
If one heard recent news during a Festival,
and at the end of the Festival it became late news,
it counts for him,
phrases.notes: The Festival days count toward the thirty days.

phrases.english: and he keeps only one day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the one-day rule for late news and applies it to a Festival case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Recent news heard on a רגל that becomes late by the end of the רגל: the רגל counts, and only one day of mourning is kept.

steps.title: The same rule for news heard on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אדא of Caesarea teaches a ברייתא before רבי יוחנן. Recent news heard on שבת that has become late by מוצאי שבת also needs only one day of mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אדא of Caesarea taught before רבי יוחנן: If one heard recent news on שבת, and at the end of שבת it became late news, he keeps only one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that applies the same idea to שבת. This backs up רבי יוסי בר אבין's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the case is שבת instead of a רגל, and again one cannot mourn openly on that day. The news was recent when he heard it on שבת. Since it became late by מוצאי שבת, he keeps only one day. The principle is the same: the day he could not mourn still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of; before (a teacher)
The end of שבת

steps.whatToRemember: Whether on a רגל or on שבת, if recent news becomes late by the time mourning is allowed, only one day is kept.

phrases.english: Rabbi Adda of Caesarea taught
before Rabbi Yochanan:
If one heard recent news on Shabbat,
and at the end of Shabbat it became late news,
he keeps only one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבִּי אַדָּא דְּמִן קֵסָרִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a parallel ברייתא about שבת that supports step 4's ruling about a רגל.
steps.raayaObject: A day when mourning is not allowed still counts toward making news late, so only one day of mourning is kept.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא taught by רבי אדא of Caesarea before רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Must one tear his garment for late news?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a person who hears late news of a death tears his garment. רבי מני says he does not, and רבי חנינא says he does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he tear his garment or not? רבי מני said: He does not tear. רבי חנינא said: He tears.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the person who hears late news (after thirty days): does he do קריעה? Two אמוראים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already learned that late news needs only one day of mourning. Now the question is about tearing, a separate mourning act. רבי מני says no tearing, and רבי חנינא says yes.

keyTerms.meaning: Tearing one's garment as a sign of mourning
He tears (his garment)
He does not tear
Late news: hearing of a death after thirty days have passed

phrases.english: Does he tear his garment or does he not tear?
Rabbi Mani said: He does not tear.
Rabbi Chanina said: He tears.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how many days late news requires to a new question: whether late news requires tearing.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether קריעה applies to someone who hears late news of a death.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מני: no tearing. רבי חנינא: tearing.

steps.title: רבי מני challenges רבי חנינא
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני says his own view makes sense, since late news has no שבעה. He then asks רבי חנינא how there can be tearing without שבעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מני said to רבי חנינא: My view makes sense. I say he does not tear, because there is no seven-day mourning here. But you say he tears. Is there ever tearing without seven days of mourning?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מני attacks רבי חנינא's view. He argues that tearing always comes together with שבעה, and late news has no שבעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key idea is that קריעה and שבעה are a package deal. Late news gets only one day of mourning, not seven, so it should get no tearing either. רבי חנינא's view seems to break this link.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (opens a contrast: 'this works, but that doesn't')
According to me ... according to you
The seven-day mourning period
Is there such a thing? (asked in a way that expects 'no')

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי מָנִי לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Mani said to Rabbi Chanina:
It makes sense according to me,
since I say he does not tear,
that is because there is no seven-day mourning.
But according to you, who says he tears,
is there such a thing as tearing without seven days?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: One side of the dispute attacks the other.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's ruling that one tears for late news.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קריעה only exists together with שבעה. Late news has no שבעה, so it cannot have קריעה.

steps.title: A ברייתא about getting a garment late
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבי מני's rule and brings a ברייתא. Someone who had no garment to tear tears it if he gets one during שבעה, but not after.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really no tearing without seven days? But a ברייתא was taught by איסי, father of רבי זירא (some say the brother of רבי זירא), in front of רבי זירא: Someone who had no shirt to tear and got one during the seven days tears it. If he got it after the seven days, he does not tear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge to רבי מני's claim that there is no tearing without שבעה. This step quotes the ברייתא and sets up the real punch, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its own, this ברייתא actually fits רבי מני: no tearing after שבעה. The challenge only works with רבי זירא's added line in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A shirt or garment
It became available to him; he got one

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the challenge is from this part of the ברייתא. This part agrees with רבי מני. The problem comes from רבי זירא's addition in the next step.

phrases.english: And is there not? But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא
by Isi, the father of Rabbi Zeira,
and some say the brother of Rabbi Zeira,
in front of Rabbi Zeira:
Someone who has no shirt to tear,
and he got one within the seven days, he tears it.
After the seven days, he does not tear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the principle רבי מני used in his attack.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מני's principle that there is no קריעה without שבעה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sets up a ברייתא whose fuller version, given in the next step, shows tearing after שבעה.

steps.title: רבי זירא adds: for parents, one keeps tearing
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא adds that the ברייתא's 'no tearing after שבעה' applies only to the other five close relatives. For a father or mother, one tears even after שבעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא added after him: When was this said? For the five relatives one must mourn. But for his father or mother, he tears even later.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the real punch of the challenge. רבי זירא says that for parents one tears even after שבעה, which seems to be tearing without seven days of mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you can tear for a parent after שבעה is over, then tearing is not always tied to שבעה. That seems to knock out רבי מני's argument against רבי חנינא.

keyTerms.meaning: He responded after him (added to what was just taught)
When is this said? (limits a rule to certain cases)
Relatives one is required to mourn
He keeps on being obligated to tear

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira responded after him:
When is this said?
For the five relatives one must mourn,
phrases.notes: He means the other close relatives: son, daughter, brother, sister, and spouse.

phrases.english: but for his father or his mother,
he keeps on tearing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun with the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מני's principle that there is no קריעה without שבעה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For a parent one tears after שבעה, so tearing can happen without seven days of mourning.

steps.title: Tearing for parents is special honor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that tearing for parents after שבעה is done to honor them. It is not regular mourning tearing, so רבי מני's rule still holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that ברייתא was taught, it was about honoring his father and mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי מני. The late tearing for parents is a special act of honor and does not show that regular קריעה can come without שבעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that all tearing is the same mourning act. The answer separates the two: normal mourning קריעה goes with שבעה, while tearing for a parent after שבעה is extra honor (כבוד אב ואם).

keyTerms.meaning: When that ברייתא was taught (it meant a specific case)
Honoring one's father and mother

steps.whatToRemember: Regular mourning tearing goes together with שבעה, so late news (with no שבעה) gets no tearing in רבי מני's view. Tearing for a parent after שבעה is a special honor, not regular mourning.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the same physical act, tearing, can come from two different reasons: mourning or honoring parents. Each has its own rules.

phrases.english: When that ברייתא was taught,
it was for the honor of his father and mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי זירא's addition and saves רבי מני's principle.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different reason: the parent case is a separate category (honor), not mourning קריעה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Tearing for a parent after שבעה shows that קריעה can exist without שבעה.
steps.terutzMaskana: That tearing is for כבוד אב ואם. Mourning קריעה still requires שבעה, so רבי מני's argument stands.

steps.title: The basic list of relatives one mourns for
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one mourns for every relative a כהן becomes impure for. It then adds a few more relatives the חכמים included.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: every relative in the כהנים passage that a כהן becomes impure for is someone a mourner mourns for. These are his wife, father, mother, brother, sister, son and daughter. The חכמים added his brother and unmarried sister from his mother, and his married sister, whether from his father or his mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא. It lists exactly which close relatives a person must mourn for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The starting point is the Torah's list of relatives for whom a כהן may become impure. The חכמים then widened mourning to include relatives a כהן would not become impure for: a brother or unmarried sister from the mother's side only, and a married sister. So the mourning list is a bit bigger than the כהן list.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah passage about which relatives a כהן may become impure for
Becomes ritually impure (here, by being near the dead)
A mourner
'They added to them.' The חכמים extended the list.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
All [the relatives] mentioned in the passage of the priests
that a priest becomes impure for them —
a mourner mourns over them,
and these are they: his wife, his father and his mother,
his brother and his sister, his son and his daughter.
phrases.notes: As in the פסוק, this means a brother from his father and an unmarried sister from his father.

phrases.english: They added to them:
his brother and his unmarried sister from his mother,
and his married sister,
whether from his father or from his mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כׇּל הָאָמוּר בְּפָרָשַׁת כֹּהֲנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of tearing for late news and opens a new topic: which relatives one mourns for.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One mourns for the seven relatives a כהן becomes impure for, plus a brother or unmarried sister from the mother and a married sister.

steps.title: Mourning for second-degree relatives: three opinions
steps.stepSummary: Three views on mourning for a relative's relatives. רבי עקיבא says yes for all of them. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says only for a grandson and a father's father. The חכמים say one mourns 'with' any relative one would mourn for.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as one mourns for those close relatives, one also mourns for their relatives. These are the words of רבי עקיבא. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says one mourns only for a son's son and a father's father. The חכמים say: anyone you would mourn for, you mourn together with when he is mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a מחלוקת. The question is whether you also mourn when a relative of your relative dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא gives the widest rule: all 'second' relatives. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר limits it to two: a grandson and a paternal grandfather. The חכמים put it differently: you join in the mourning of any close relative who is now a mourner.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Second ones': second-degree relatives, meaning the relatives of your close relatives
His son's son (grandson)
His father's father
Mourns together with him

phrases.english: And just as he mourns over them —
so he mourns over their second ones,
phrases.notes: This means their own close relatives. For example, his father's father, or his brother's son.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ מִתְאַבֵּל אֶלָּא עַל בֶּן בְּנוֹ
phrases.english: He mourns only over his son's son
and over his father's father.
And the Sages say:
Anyone over whom he would mourn, he mourns with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֵׁם שֶׁמִּתְאַבֵּל עֲלֵיהֶם כָּךְ מִתְאַבֵּל עַל שְׁנִיִּים שֶׁלָּהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, moving from close relatives to second-degree relatives.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא: mourn for all second-degree relatives. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: only a grandson and a paternal grandfather. חכמים: mourn together with any relative you would mourn for.

steps.title: Isn't the view of the חכמים the same as רבי עקיבא's?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the חכמים add. Their view seems to say the same thing as רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The view of the חכמים is the same as the first תנא's view!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. The חכמים seem to be repeating רבי עקיבא, so what is the difference? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רבי עקיבא and the חכמים end up with mourning when a close relative's relative dies. If the rule is the same, why list it as a separate opinion? The גמרא wants a practical difference between them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That is the same as.' Used to ask why two opinions are counted as different.
The first תנא, the opinion stated first (here, רבי עקיבא)

phrases.english: The Sages are the same as the first Tanna?
phrases.notes: The 'first תנא' here is רבי עקיבא, whose view was stated first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the difference between two opinions in the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of the חכמים in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their rule seems to give the same result as רבי עקיבא's, so it does not look like a separate opinion.

steps.title: The difference: being in the same house
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the difference is 'with him' in the house. The חכמים require mourning only when you are with the mourner.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: 'with him' means in the house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The חכמים are different from רבי עקיבא because of the word 'with him.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say 'mourns with him,' which means only while you are together with the mourner in the same house. רבי עקיבא requires mourning for second-degree relatives even when you are not with the mourner. So the two views are not the same.

keyTerms.meaning: 'There is between them': the practical difference between two views
With him in the house: in the mourner's presence

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'with him' as just 'also.' It is the whole point: according to the חכמים, the mourning applies only while you are physically together with the mourner.

phrases.english: There is [a difference] between them:
"with him" in the house.
phrases.notes: The חכמים want mourning only while you're with the mourner. רבי עקיבא wants it even when you're apart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out a practical difference between the two views
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים and רבי עקיבא seem to rule the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים require mourning only in the mourner's presence. רבי עקיבא requires it always.

steps.title: רב and רב הונא: mourn only in her presence
steps.stepSummary: רב and רב הונא told their sons, whose wives were mourning, to mourn in front of their wives but not when away from them. This matches the חכמים' 'in the house' rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רב told his son חייא, and what רב הונא told his son רבה: in her presence, act as a mourner; not in her presence, do not act as a mourner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real-life ruling that shows the 'with him in the house' idea in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sons' wives were in mourning. The fathers told them to join the mourning only when they were with their wives. This is exactly the חכמים' view: you join a relative's mourning only in that relative's presence.

keyTerms.meaning: In her presence (literally, 'before her face')
Practice mourning
'Like this': introduces an example that fits the rule

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ רַב לְחִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Like that which Rav said to Ḥiyya his son,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא לְרַבָּה בְּרֵיהּ:
phrases.english: and similarly Rav Huna said to Rabba his son:
In her presence, practice mourning;
phrases.notes: 'Her' is the son's wife, who was in mourning.

phrases.english: not in her presence, do not practice mourning.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ רַב לְחִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the 'in the house' rule from step 14 was followed in practice.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one mourns with a relative only in that relative's presence
steps.raayaSupportSource: The instructions of רב and רב הונא to their sons
steps.whatToRemember: According to the חכמים, joining a relative's mourning applies only while you are together with that mourner.

steps.title: מר עוקבא starts mourning for his brother-in-law
steps.stepSummary: מר עוקבא's brother-in-law died. He planned to keep the full שבעה and שלושים, and רב הונא came and found him mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר עוקבא's father-in-law's son died. He thought to sit שבעה and שלושים for him. רב הונא came to him and found him mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about מר עוקבא. This sets up רב הונא's ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dead man was the brother of מר עוקבא's wife. מר עוקבא thought that, for his wife's sake, he should keep full mourning. The story is building toward whether that is really required.

keyTerms.meaning: His father-in-law's son, meaning his brother-in-law
The seven-day and thirty-day mourning periods
He found him

phrases.aramaic: מָר עוּקְבָא שְׁכֵיב לֵיהּ בַּר חֲמוּהּ.
phrases.english: Mar Ukva: his father-in-law's son died.
He thought to sit over him for seven and thirty [days],
Rav Huna came in to him and found him [mourning],

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר עוּקְבָא שְׁכֵיב לֵיהּ בַּר חֲמוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that tests how far mourning for a wife's family goes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: a man is mourning fully for his wife's brother.

steps.title: רב הונא: for your wife's sake, only her parents
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא tells מר עוקבא he does not need to mourn. Mourning for a wife's sake applies only for her father or mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'Do you want to eat mourners' food?!' They only said to mourn in honor of one's wife when her father or her mother dies.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא corrects מר עוקבא. He sets a limit on mourning for a wife's family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule says you mourn with a mourning relative in her presence. But for a wife, this applies only when she mourns her parents, your father-in-law and mother-in-law. It does not apply to her brother, so מר עוקבא's full שבעה and שלושים were not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Mourners' food (said sharply, as in 'are you looking to eat mourners' meals?')
In honor of his wife
His father-in-law and mother-in-law

steps.whatToRemember: A husband joins his wife's mourning only for her parents, not for her other relatives like a brother.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a practical limit on 'mourning with' a relative when it comes to a wife: her parents count, her siblings do not.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Do you want to eat mourners' food?!
They did not say [to mourn] in honor of his wife —
except [for] his father-in-law and his mother-in-law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב הונא's ruling on the story in step 16. It rejects מר עוקבא's plan to mourn.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Mourning in honor of one's wife applies only when her father or mother died, not her brother.

steps.title: A ברייתא: husband and wife mourn together for each other's parents
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that when a man's in-laws die, he must mourn together with his wife. The same is true for her when his parents die.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: If a man's father-in-law or mother-in-law died, he may not make his wife paint her eyes or put makeup on her face. Instead, he turns over his bed and mourns with her. In the same way, if her father-in-law or mother-in-law died, she may not paint her eyes or put on makeup. Instead, she turns over her bed and mourns with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רב הונא's rule. That rule says you mourn for your spouse's sake only when the spouse's father or mother died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא talks only about the spouse's parents (חמיו וחמותו). In that case the husband must actually keep mourning practices himself, such as overturning his bed. This matches רב הונא's ruling that mourning for a wife's sake applies to her father or mother.

keyTerms.meaning: His father-in-law and mother-in-law (his wife's parents)
Painting the eyes with eye makeup
Putting color or rouge on the face
Overturns his bed, an old mourning practice
Mourning practices

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: מִי שֶׁמֵּת חָמִיו אוֹ חֲמוֹתוֹ —
phrases.english: As it is taught: one whose father-in-law or mother-in-law died —
may not force his wife
to paint her eyes or to put rouge on her face,
rather, he overturns his bed,
and keeps mourning together with her.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הִיא שֶׁמֵּת חָמִיהָ אוֹ חֲמוֹתָהּ —
phrases.english: And likewise she, whose father-in-law or mother-in-law died —

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָהּ רַשָּׁאָה לִהְיוֹת כּוֹחֶלֶת וְלִהְיוֹת פּוֹקֶסֶת,
phrases.english: she may not paint her eyes or put rouge on her face,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כּוֹפָה מִטָּתָהּ וְנוֹהֶגֶת עִמּוֹ אֲבֵילוּת.
phrases.english: rather, she overturns her bed and keeps mourning together with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: מִי שֶׁמֵּת חָמִיו אוֹ חֲמוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ברייתא source for רב הונא's ruling in step 17
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's rule that mourning for a wife's sake applies only to her father or mother
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא requiring a spouse to mourn together with the other spouse for the death of a parent-in-law

steps.title: A second ברייתא seems to contradict the first
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says the mourning wife may still pour her husband's cup, make his bed, and wash him. This suggests he is not mourning with her, which clashes with the first ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: Even though they said a man may not force his wife to paint her eyes or put on makeup, the truth is they said she may pour his cup, make his bed for him, and wash his face, hands, and feet. These two ברייתות contradict each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a second ברייתא and points out that it seems to clash with the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא says the husband must mourn together with his wife. The second ברייתא only forbids him to push her to dress up. It does not require him to mourn at all, and she keeps serving him as usual. So the two sources seem to disagree about whether the husband mourns with her.

keyTerms.meaning: In truth they said, a phrase introducing a set law
Pours or mixes a drink
They contradict each other

phrases.english: And another ברייתא teaches:
Even though they said
he may not force his wife
to paint her eyes or put rouge on her face,

phrases.aramaic: בֶּאֱמֶת אָמְרוּ מוֹזֶגֶת לוֹ אֶת הַכּוֹס,
phrases.english: in truth they said she may pour his cup for him,
and make his bed for him,
and wash his face, hands, and feet.
They contradict each other!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a second ברייתא against the one just quoted
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about a husband mourning with his wife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One ברייתא requires the husband to mourn with his wife, while the other implies life goes on normally for him, so they seem to clash.

steps.title: Two different cases: in-laws versus other relatives
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles the clash. The first ברייתא is about the spouse's parents, and the second is about the wife's other relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: Must we not learn from this: here it is about his father-in-law and mother-in-law, and there it is about other relatives? Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by assigning each ברייתא to a different kind of relative.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the wife's parents die, the husband mourns with her, as the first ברייתא says. When other relatives of hers die, he does not mourn himself. He only may not push her to dress up, as the second ברייתא says. This matches רב הונא's rule exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Must we not conclude from this?
Here... there; each source deals with a different case
Other relatives

steps.whatToRemember: A husband keeps mourning practices for his wife's sake only for her father or mother. For her other relatives he does not mourn, though he cannot push her to stop mourning.

phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from this:
here, it is about his father-in-law and mother-in-law,
phrases.notes: "Here" is the first ברייתא, where he mourns with her.

phrases.english: there, it is about other relatives.
Yes, learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: כָּאן בְּחָמִיו וַחֲמוֹתוֹ, כָּאן בִּשְׁאָר קְרוֹבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ברייתא speaks about a different relative
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to speak about the same situation, so they seemed to clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first ברייתא is about the wife's parents, where the husband mourns. The second is about her other relatives, where he does not mourn.

steps.title: Another ברייתא confirms: only for her parents
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says openly that mourning for a wife's honor applies only to her father and mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: They said a man mourns for his wife's honor only for his father-in-law and mother-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more ברייתא that states the conclusion outright.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 reached the rule by working it out from two sources. Here a ברייתא says it plainly: mourning out of honor for one's wife is limited to her parents.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this, offering support
For the honor of his wife
Only

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
They did not say to mourn for his wife's honor
except for his father-in-law and mother-in-law only.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 20 with an open statement
steps.raayaObject: The rule that mourning for a wife's sake applies only to her parents

steps.title: אמימר tears his clothes again in front of his son, then again standing
steps.stepSummary: When אמימר's grandson died, he tore his clothes. He tore again when his son came, and once more standing up after remembering he had torn while sitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר's grandson died, and he tore his garment over him. His son came, and he tore again in front of him. He remembered that he had torn while sitting, so he stood up and tore while standing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about אמימר that continues the theme of mourning for the sake of a close relative.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמימר had already torn for his grandson. He tore again in front of his son because his son was the main mourner and the grieving father. He then tore once more because the tearing in front of his son had been done sitting, and he redid it standing.

keyTerms.meaning: Tearing one's garment as a sign of mourning
His son's son (his grandson)
In his presence, in front of him
Sitting / standing

steps.confusionAlert: אמימר tore three times: once for his grandson, again in front of his son, and a third time to redo the second one standing. It was not three separate deaths.

phrases.english: אמימר's son's son died,
he tore his garment over him.
His son came, and he tore in front of him.
phrases.notes: This son is the father of the child who died, so he is the main mourner.

phrases.english: He remembered that he had torn while sitting,
so he stood up and tore while standing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from mourning for a wife's sake to a story about mourning in front of a grieving son
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person mourns again in front of a close relative who is grieving, and tearing the garment is done while standing.

steps.title: רב אשי asks for the source of tearing while standing
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks אמימר what source teaches that קריעה must be done standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: From where do we learn that tearing must be done while standing?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks אמימר for the source of the rule he just followed, tearing while standing. This question sets up אמימר's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 22 אמימר tore a second time because his first tear was done sitting. That shows he holds that קריעה must be done standing. רב אשי is not arguing; he wants to know what the rule is based on.

keyTerms.meaning: Tearing one's clothing as a sign of mourning
Standing
From where do we know this? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
Tearing while standing, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the practice shown in אמימר's story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that קריעה must be done while standing.

steps.title: אמימר answers from the פסוק about איוב
steps.stepSummary: אמימר brings the פסוק that איוב stood up and then tore his coat.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "Then איוב arose, and tore his coat."
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר answers רב אשי's question with a פסוק from איוב. Since איוב stood up and then tore, we learn that קריעה is done standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is in the order of the words: first "he arose," then "he tore." This shows that the tearing happened while standing, so it becomes the model for every mourner's קריעה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (introduces a פסוק)
And he arose / stood up
His coat / outer garment

steps.whatToRemember: קריעה for a mourner is done standing. We learn this from איוב, who stood up and then tore his coat.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why אמימר re-tore while standing, and it gives a source for how קריעה is done in practice.

phrases.english: As it is written: "Then Job arose,
and tore his coat."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers רב אשי's question from step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק says איוב stood up and then tore his coat, which shows that קריעה is done standing.
